title: Prudent Corporate Advisory Services Ltd - 543527 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Prudent's Q1 FY27 is a distributor-platform growth story, not a capital-cycle one: equity AUM up 18% to INR1.34 lakh crore, but gross yield slipped to ~88 bps and commission payout fell after a regulatory reset.

summary.headline: Prudent's Q1 FY27 PAT rose 44.4% YoY to INR74.8 crores, with average AUM up 21% to INR1.33 lakh crores despite a 2.8 bps gross yield cut.
summary.overview: Prudent reported Q1 FY27 with average AUM of INR1.33 lakh crores (up 21% YoY, 4% QoQ) and equity AUM of INR1.34 lakh crores as of June 2026. Operating profit rose 32.4% YoY to INR89.1 crores and PAT rose 44.4% YoY to INR74.8 crores, helped by treasury gains. New SEBI/AMC regulatory changes from April 2026 (GST treatment, exit load removal) cut gross yield by about 2.8 bps to around 88 bps and shifted commission expense lower, which management called a one-time reset. Management said the current margin should be the run-rate for the next three quarters.

financial_highlights.change: ~16% above FY26 average AUM of INR1.21 lakh crores
+18% YoY from INR1.14 lakh crores; +16.4% QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Gross yield on MF average AUM
financial_highlights.change: down ~2.8 bps from 91.2 bps last quarter

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Average PMS AUM grew 37% YoY to about INR1,900 crores (PMS+AIF combined). SIF AUM crossed INR500 crores with about 1,323 to 1,400 SIF-certified MFDs. Management does not report segment margins.

segments.name: Life insurance
segments.commentary: Fresh premium grew 73.4% YoY, with participating plans up 100% and ULIP up 82%.

segments.name: Other financial and non-financial products
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 28.4% YoY, driven by PMS and bond distribution; bond distribution income more than doubled YoY.

guidance_outlook: Gross yield expected to be maintained at around 88 bps; new business yield slightly higher than existing book; management said current quarter margin can be used as run-rate for next three quarters.
Employee cost growth expected at 22% to 24% for FY27 including ESOP expense; about 30 new branches planned in FY27, with more than 12 already operational in Q1.
Other expenses are seasonal and volatile (linked to insurance mobilisation marketing); management declined to give an annual growth estimate.
Management said it remains very optimistic about FY27 overall.
Mutual fund yield expected to fall by 1 to 2 bps over the medium to long term, mainly on new business; no major change expected in the current year.
Investors should look at consolidated numbers only, as business is being merged into Prudent Corporate; standalone numbers no longer representative.
capex_capacity: About 30 new branches planned for FY27, with more than 12 operationalised in Q1 FY27.
Treasury book of about INR650 crores; management evaluating acquisitions to strengthen the distribution platform.
Indus acquisition completed in September (2025), contributing to equity AUM growth.
demand_pricing: Net sales of INR3,790 crores in Q1 FY27, roughly in line with the ~INR3,700 crore quarterly run rate of the last 3-4 quarters; management says market share versus industry has risen even as industry net sales fell.

Monthly MFD partner additions averaged about 600 per month in Q1 FY27 versus 430 per month in FY26; registrations up 45-50% in the last 3.5 months, mostly from existing distributors moving to the platform.
About 60% of AUM is mobilised through GST-registered partners and about 40% through non-GST-registered partners as of June 2026.
Direct versus indirect split of AUM is roughly 90:10 (90% served via partners).
Management views the SEBI proposal for mutual-fund-only PMS at a INR25 lakh ticket size as a possible opportunity; not yet discussed at the Board level and no PMS licence decision taken.
Management expects no yield improvement from mutual-fund-only PMS, citing competitive pressure.

qa_highlights.question: What was the gross margin last quarter and how has it moved this quarter, and what is the standalone MF contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Shah said MF margin was 91.2 bps last quarter and about 88.4 bps this quarter, a 2.8 bps fall due to the 5 bps exit load removal from TER. Segment margins are not disclosed; operating margin is the suggested proxy.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 commission-to-revenue ratio (56.2% standalone) a steady-state number?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Shah said the current margin can be used for the next three quarters and the spread should hold, as the regulatory changes were applied across the full book. Shirish Patel added that insurance mix in Q4 was higher, which also affects the ratio.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net revenue yield after commissions and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said current yield levels would likely persist in the near term; medium to long term it could fall 1 to 2 bps, mainly on new business.

qa_highlights.question: Can MFD partners go direct once mutual-fund-only PMS is allowed?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said the risk is low since MFDs need a platform; a possible consolidation of licences is the bigger effect. No yield uplift is assumed from the 2.25% PMS fee structure.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the new MFD additions and what is the direct versus indirect AUM split?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said most of the increase in registrations came from existing distributors moving to Prudent's platform. Sanjay Shah put the split at roughly 90:10 (partners versus direct).

qa_highlights.question: How should AUM growth be viewed beyond MTM, and how fast is net sales growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said net sales historically add about 10-12% to AUM each year, and FY26 growth came mainly from net sales rather than MTM.

risks_watch: Gross yield: management guides ~88 bps for the year, but says medium-to-long-term MF yield could fall 1-2 bps, mainly on new business; track the monthly yield trend against the 88.4 bps Q1 figure.

Commission payout: the commission-to-revenue ratio (56.2% standalone) and the net spread are described as steady for three quarters; check whether the GST pass-through benefit persists given ~40% of AUM sits with non-GST partners.
Employee cost growth guided at 22-24% for FY27 including ESOP, with ~30 branches planned (12+ done in Q1); watch whether operating margin holds as branch expansion continues.
Other expenses are seasonal and volatile (insurance mobilisation marketing) with no annual growth estimate, so quarterly operating profit may be lumpy.
PAT growth (44.4%) was helped by treasury gains; underlying profit growth (operating profit +32.4%) is the cleaner measure to track.
Net sales of ~INR3,790 crores are flat versus the ~INR3,700 crore run rate; management claims share gains versus a weak industry, so monitor net sales and the 10-12% AUM net-sales contribution.
SEBI consultation on mutual-fund-only PMS at INR25 lakh ticket size: no Board discussion or licence decision yet; management sees no yield uplift and flags possible distributor licence consolidation.
Standalone numbers are no longer representative as business merges into Prudent Corporate; investors are asked to use consolidated figures only.
key_quotes: So I think this is the average of impact which we have on account of entire book, which has been repriced from 1st of April.

Please note, we view this as a one-time reset. With this transition now complete, the gross profit margin reported during the quarter reflects the economics of the business under the revised regulatory framework.
So regarding the margin, I tell you, you can probably consider the current quarter as a representative of margin.
Sanjay Shah: Yes. I just wanted to tell you now you should look at only consolidated because the business is also getting merged in the Prudent Corporate.
I don't see that I think the overall yield should improve because of this particular product because I think this is also a very, very competitive space
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on AUM, SIP flows and distributor additions, and said it remains very optimistic about FY27. It was more cautious and evasive on segment margins (not disclosed), other-expense trajectory (\"very difficult to quantify\") and the yield impact of the proposed PMS regime, where it assumed no uplift.

adds.what: About 30 new branches in FY27 (more than 12 already operational in Q1 FY27)

growth.why: Revenue from operations grew 18.3% YoY and average AUM rose 21% YoY, with about 30 new branches planned in FY27 (over 12 already operational) and management "very optimistic" about FY27; however, gross yield is being cut and no capacity utilisation figure or segment margin was given, so the outlook is moderate rather than strong.
